name: Daisy Down-Set and Zero-Defect Equivalence
hypotheses: Nonempty finite binary class, interpreted up to coordinate permutations and bit complements.
statement: A class has a rooted down-set representation if and only if its daisy completion defect vanishes, and if and only if its edge defect vanishes.
proof: The equality $\delta_D(C)=0$ says directly that $C=D_r(C)$ for some root. The equality $\eta(C)=0$ says that some orientation toward a minimizing root has no missing inward edge; repeated inward steps then show that $C$ is the rooted down-set $D_r(C)$.
